title: Is doodling good for you
titleChinese: 心不在焉地随手乱画对你有好处吗？
paragraphs: Do you sometimes find yourself drawing random patterns and designs during meetings and lectures? Some people believe it shows you aren’t listening or paying attention. However, there are studies which claim the opposite, and that doodling might actually be beneficial.

Doodling seems to be ubiquitous. In the past it was seen as a mindless activity and a product of the absentminded. However, in 2016, an article on the Harvard University website discussed the idea that random drawings may assist memory retention and concentration.

The article highlights that 26 of 44 American presidents were known to doodle, with Ronald Reagan famous for drawing cowboys. A 2009 study conducted by psychologist Jackie Andrade asked 40 people to listen to a ‘dull and rambling’ voice message. Half of the group were asked to doodle and shade in a picture. Those who did were able to recall 29% more of the information contained in the message.

Some experts believe that embracing your creative and artistic sides during meetings may engage your mind. Jesse Prinz, a renowned professor of philosophy, actively encourages his students to doodle. He believes that doodling is the ‘attentional sweet spot’.

And it might not just be good for your concentration. An artist known as Mr Doodle has made a career out of his scribbles. He sells his art online and also goes to people’s homes to decorate their walls.

It seems that random drawing to aid concentration might be becoming more of a thing. People like Sunni Brown, an advocate for doodling, teach adults how to sketch and scribble in the workplace. So, the next time you see someone haphazardly drawing pictures during a meeting, it might be a sign that they are listening more than you think.

vocabulary.entry: random pattern /ˈrændəm ˈpætn/ 随意的图案
vocabulary.example: She likes to draw random pattern when she is thinking.
vocabulary.translation: 她思考的时候喜欢画些随意的图案。

vocabulary.entry: doodle /ˈduːdl/ v. 随手涂鸦；信手乱画
vocabulary.example: He tends to doodle when he's on the phone.
vocabulary.translation: 他打电话的时候总爱随手涂鸦。

vocabulary.entry: beneficial /ˌbenɪˈfɪʃl/ adj. 有益的；有利的
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise is beneficial to health.
vocabulary.translation: 规律运动对健康有益。

vocabulary.entry: ubiquitous /juːˈbɪkwɪtəs/ adj. 无处不在的；十分普遍的
vocabulary.example: Smartphones have become ubiquitous in modern life.
vocabulary.translation: 智能手机在现代生活中已经变得无处不在。

vocabulary.entry: mindless activity /ˈmaɪndləs ækˈtɪvəti/ 无意识的举动；无需动脑的行为
vocabulary.example: Chewing gum is a mindless activity that many people do daily.
vocabulary.translation: 嚼口香糖是许多人每天都会做的一种无需动脑的行为。

vocabulary.entry: absentminded /ˌæbsənˈmaɪndɪd/ adj. 心不在焉的；走神的
vocabulary.example: The absentminded student forgot to bring his textbook to class.
vocabulary.translation: 这个心不在焉的学生忘了带课本去上课。

vocabulary.entry: memory retention /ˈmeməri rɪˈtenʃn/ 记忆力；记忆保持能力
vocabulary.example: Regular review is key to improving memory retention.
vocabulary.translation: 定期复习是提升记忆保持能力的关键。

vocabulary.entry: concentration /ˌkɒnsnˈtreɪʃn/ n. 专注力；注意力
vocabulary.example: It's hard to maintain concentration with so much noise around.
vocabulary.translation: 周围这么吵，很难集中注意力。

vocabulary.entry: highlight /ˈhaɪlaɪt/ v. 强调；突出显示
vocabulary.example: The report highlights the importance of protecting the environment.
vocabulary.translation: 这份报告强调了保护环境的重要性。

vocabulary.entry: dull and rambling /dʌl ənd ˈræmblɪŋ/ 枯燥冗长的
vocabulary.example: The audience was bored by his dull and rambling speech.
vocabulary.translation: 他的演讲枯燥冗长，让听众感到很无聊。

vocabulary.entry: voice message /vɔɪs ˈmesɪdʒ/ 语音信息
vocabulary.example: I left a voice message for my colleague this morning.
vocabulary.translation: 我今早给同事留了一条语音信息。

vocabulary.entry: shade /ʃeɪd/ v. 给……上色；为……填色
vocabulary.example: The children were asked to shade the pictures with crayons.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们被要求用蜡笔给这些画上色。

vocabulary.entry: recall /rɪˈkɔːl/ v. 回忆起；记起
vocabulary.example: I can't recall where I put my keys.
vocabulary.translation: 我想不起来把钥匙放哪儿了。

vocabulary.entry: embrace /ɪmˈbreɪs/ v. 发挥；接纳
vocabulary.example: We should embrace our differences and learn from each other.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该接纳彼此的差异，互相学习。

vocabulary.entry: renowned /rɪˈnaʊnd/ adj. 著名的；有名望的
vocabulary.example: She is a renowned expert in the field of neuroscience.
vocabulary.translation: 她是神经科学领域的知名专家。

vocabulary.entry: attentional sweet spot /əˈtenʃənl swiːt spɒt/ 注意力最佳状态
vocabulary.example: The researcher claims that moderate music can help reach the attentional sweet spot.
vocabulary.translation: 这位研究者称，舒缓的音乐有助于进入注意力最佳状态。

vocabulary.entry: scribble /ˈskrɪbl/ n. 随手画的潦草图案
vocabulary.example: The notebook was full of scribbles and notes.
vocabulary.translation: 这本笔记本上满是潦草的涂鸦和笔记。

vocabulary.entry: make a career out of /meɪk ə kəˈrɪə aʊt ɒv/ 靠……开创事业
vocabulary.example: He made a career out of his passion for photography.
vocabulary.translation: 他靠自己对摄影的热爱开创了一番事业。

vocabulary.entry: advocate /ˈædvəkət/ n. 倡导者；支持者
vocabulary.example: She is a strong advocate for women's rights.
vocabulary.translation: 她是妇女权利的坚定倡导者。

vocabulary.entry: sketch /sketʃ/ v. 画草图；速写
vocabulary.example: The artist likes to sketch people on the street.
vocabulary.translation: 这位艺术家喜欢在街上给路人画速写。

vocabulary.entry: haphazardly /həˈpæzədli/ adv. 随意地；杂乱无章地
vocabulary.example: He haphazardly threw his clothes on the chair.
vocabulary.translation: 他随手把衣服扔在了椅子上。

vocabulary.entry: aid /eɪd/ v. 帮助；辅助
vocabulary.example: This software can aid in data analysis.
vocabulary.translation: 这款软件可以辅助进行数据分析。

sentences.english: Do you sometimes find yourself drawing random patterns and designs during meetings and lectures?
sentences.chinese: 你是否有时会在开会或听讲座时，不自觉地画些随意的图案和纹样？

sentences.english: Some people believe it shows you aren’t listening or paying attention.
sentences.chinese: 有些人认为这是心不在焉、没有认真听讲的表现。

sentences.english: However, there are studies which claim the opposite, and that doodling might actually be beneficial.
sentences.chinese: 但有研究却得出了相反的结论，认为涂鸦实际上可能是有益的。
涂鸦这种行为似乎无处不在。

sentences.english: In the past it was seen as a mindless activity and a product of the absentminded.
sentences.chinese: 在过去，它被视为一种无意识的举动，是心不在焉的产物。

sentences.english: However, in 2016, an article on the Harvard University website discussed the idea that random drawings may assist memory retention and concentration.
sentences.chinese: 但2016年哈佛大学官网上的一篇文章指出，随手涂鸦有助于增强记忆力和专注力。

sentences.english: The article highlights that 26 of 44 American presidents were known to doodle, with Ronald Reagan famous for drawing cowboys.
sentences.chinese: 这篇文章还提到，美国44任总统中有26位都有涂鸦的习惯，其中罗纳德·里根就因画牛仔而闻名。

sentences.english: A 2009 study conducted by psychologist Jackie Andrade asked 40 people to listen to a ‘dull and rambling’ voice message.
sentences.chinese: 2009年，心理学家杰姬·安德拉德开展了一项研究，她让40人聆听一段“枯燥冗长”的语音信息。

sentences.english: Half of the group were asked to doodle and shade in a picture. Those who did were able to recall 29% more of the information contained in the message.
sentences.chinese: 研究人员要求其中一半人边听边涂鸦并给图案上色，结果发现这部分人能多回忆起29%的信息。

sentences.english: Some experts believe that embracing your creative and artistic sides during meetings may engage your mind.
sentences.chinese: 一些专家认为，在开会时发挥自己的创意和艺术天赋，能让大脑保持活跃状态。

sentences.english: Jesse Prinz, a renowned professor of philosophy, actively encourages his students to doodle. He believes that doodling is the ‘attentional sweet spot’.
sentences.chinese: 著名哲学教授杰西·普林茨就积极鼓励学生涂鸦，他认为涂鸦是“注意力的最佳状态”。

sentences.english: And it might not just be good for your concentration.
sentences.chinese: 而且涂鸦的好处可能不止提升专注力这一点。

sentences.english: An artist known as Mr Doodle has made a career out of his scribbles.
sentences.chinese: 一位名叫“涂鸦先生”的艺术家就靠自己的随手涂鸦开创了一番事业。

sentences.english: He sells his art online and also goes to people’s homes to decorate their walls.
sentences.chinese: 他不仅在网上售卖自己的作品，还会上门帮人装饰墙面。

sentences.english: It seems that random drawing to aid concentration might be becoming more of a thing.
sentences.chinese: 如今，用随手涂鸦来提升专注力的做法似乎越来越流行。

sentences.english: People like Sunni Brown, an advocate for doodling, teach adults how to sketch and scribble in the workplace.
sentences.chinese: 桑妮·布朗等涂鸦倡导者还会教成年人如何在工作场合随手画些草图和涂鸦。

sentences.english: So, the next time you see someone haphazardly drawing pictures during a meeting, it might be a sign that they are listening more than you think.
sentences.chinese: 所以下次再看到有人在开会时随意画画，这或许恰恰说明他们比你想象中听得更认真。
